# @buildanagent/agent-safety

> Safety core for buildanagent agents: typed write outcomes the model can read, a canonical input hash, signed approvals, model calls on the user's own key and a USD cap checked before each model call.

The sections of README.md and every public export, generated from this package's README and declaration files in the same commit as its code.

## Exports from `@buildanagent/agent-safety`

- `ALLOWED_RETRIES`: The retry rules each kind allows, as `AllowedRetry` lists them.
- `interface AllowedRetry`: The retry rules each outcome kind allows.
- `interface ApprovalSigner`: Signs and verifies the payload of a pending request.
- `canonicalInputHash()`: Hashes a tool input: the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON (RFC 8785), as 64 lowercase hex digits.
- `checkModelRoutes()`: Checks the model routes a deploy configures and reports every problem, so a deploy gate can fail on any of them.
- `CLOUDFLARE_AI_GATEWAY_HOST`: The host of Cloudflare AI Gateway's provider endpoints, as in `https://gateway.ai.cloudflare.com/v1/…`.
- `CLOUDFLARE_GATEWAY_TOKEN_HEADER`: The header that carries the token of a Cloudflare AI Gateway with authentication turned on.
- `CLOUDFLARE_NO_WHOLESALE_HEADER`: The header that tells Cloudflare AI Gateway never to bill a request to Cloudflare's own credentials.
- `interface CloudflareAiGatewaySettings`: The Cloudflare AI Gateway settings a route through that gateway must record.
- `CREDENTIAL_HEADERS`: Headers that carry a credential for some model provider or gateway.
- `type CredentialHeader`: The header that carries a provider's key: `x-api-key` for Anthropic, `authorization` for OpenAI.
- `DEFAULT_RETRY`: The retry rule each kind gets when the tool sets none: a rejected write may run again with the same key, an undone one only as a new operation, a partial one goes to a person, and an unknown one is checked first.
- `type EffectClaim`: What `begin()` and `takeOver()` return: `"started"` if the caller now holds the record, or the record that won.
- `effectKey()`: Returns the effect key of a write, as 64 lowercase hex digits.
- `interface EffectRecord`: One write's entry in the effects ledger.
- `interface EffectScope`: Where a write was asked for: the tenant, the session and branch of the conversation, and the model's tool call.
- `interface EffectStore`: Stores effect records by key.
- `interface EgressCredential`: The one credential a guarded request must carry.
- `egressGuard()`: Wraps `fetch` so a model request leaves only for `baseURL` and only with `credential`.
- `interface EgressGuardOptions`: The options of `egressGuard()`.
- `ephemeralSigner()`: A signer whose key is random and lives only in this process: every call in one process returns the same signer, and no other process can verify what it signs.
- `guardedWrite()`: Runs a write at most once per effect key.
- `interface GuardedWriteOptions`: The options of `guardedWrite()`.
- `hmacSigner()`: A signer over a key ring, for any host where a pause may resume in another process: it signs with the key named `current` and verifies with any key in `keys`.
- `interface HmacSignerOptions`: The options of `hmacSigner()`: every key the signer may verify with, by id, and the id of the one it signs with.
- `isSafetyError()`: True for a `SafetyError`, including one from another copy of the package.
- `interface KeyRing`: A key ring: every key a signer may verify with, by id, and the id of the key that signs.
- `interface KeyStore`: A host's key ring store.
- `lintPlan()`: Checks the order of a plan's steps: every compensable step comes before the pivot, a plan has at most one pivot, and every retryable step comes after it, so a plan without a pivot holds compensable steps only.
- `memoryEffectStore()`: An `EffectStore` in this process's memory, for tests and single-process hosts.
- `memoryPendingStore()`: A `PendingStore` in this process's memory, for tests and single-process hosts.
- `interface MemoryPendingStoreOptions`: The options of `memoryPendingStore()`.
- `memoryPlanLedger()`: A `PlanLedger` that keeps each plan's progress in memory, for tests and single-process hosts.
- `MIN_KEY_BYTES`: The shortest key `hmacSigner()` accepts: one SHA-256 output, the length RFC 2104 recommends as the minimum.
- `MODEL_ROUTE_SETTINGS_AS_OF`: The date of the gateway documentation the checker's setting names come from: Cloudflare AI Gateway's Unified Billing page (`byok_only`, "Require provider credentials") and Vercel AI Gateway's BYOK page ("Fallback to Vercel Keys").
- `interface ModelRoute`: One model route a deploy configures: which provider, at which base URL, and the gateway's settings if it has one.
- `interface ModelRouteProblem`: One reason a configuration failed.
- `type ModelRouteProblemCode`: Why a configuration failed.
- `type ModelRouteProvider`: The providers a model route may name.
- `interface ModelRoutesConfig`: The model routes a deploy step produces, which `checkModelRoutes()` reads.
- `interface ModelRoutesReport`: What `checkModelRoutes()` found.
- `OUTCOME_KINDS`: The five outcome kinds, in the order the docs list them.
- `interface OutcomeFields`: The fields every write outcome carries, whatever its kind.
- `type OutcomeKind`: What a write did.
- `type OutcomePayload`: The structured half of a rendered outcome: the outcome's own fields, as plain JSON.
- `parseKeyRing()`: Reads a key ring from JSON text such as a secret's value: `{"current":"2026-11","keys":{"2026-11":"<key>"}}`, where each key is base64url without padding.
- `interface PendingCall`: The call a host is about to run, which a pending request must match before it runs.
- `interface PendingFields`: The fields `signPending()` signs and stores, with the call's input in place of its hash.
- `pendingPayload()`: The bytes a pending request's signature covers: a JSON array of a fixed tag, then the request id, kind, call id, tool name, input hash and policy version, in that order, with `null` for an absent policy version.
- `interface PendingStore`: Holds signed pending requests by call id.
- `interface PlanApproval`: A signed plan approval.
- `planCard()`: Builds the approval card for a plan, from the same fields you will pass to `signPlan()` once the person approves.
- `interface PlanCard`: The approval card's payload: the steps in the order they run, the pivot's id, and the state the plan read.
- `interface PlanCardStep`: One step as the approval card shows it.
- `type PlanFailureReason`: Why a plan that began could not finish.
- `interface PlanFields`: The plan a person approved: its steps, the state it was computed from, and how long the approval lasts.
- `interface PlanLedger`: Records which steps of each plan have passed verification.
- `type PlanLint`: What `lintPlan()` returns: `ok`, or every problem it found with the order of the steps.
- `type PlanOutcome`: What a plan did, computed by the harness and never by the model.
- `type PlanScope`: Where a plan runs: the tenant, session and branch its writes are keyed under.
- `interface PlanStep`: One signed step of a plan: its tool and the hash of its exact input, with a summary for the approval card.
- `interface PlanStepCall`: The step a host is about to run, as it has the step now, not as the approval records it.
- `type PlanStepCheck`: What `verifyPlanBeforeStep()` found.
- `interface PlanStepImpl`: One signed step as the host runs it: the step, its exact input and the calls that perform and undo it.
- `interface PlanStepInit`: A step as the host plans it, with its input in place of the input's hash.
- `planWriteOutcome()`: The write outcome a plan outcome stands for, in the five kinds the model already reads: `completed` is `applied`, `failed_compensated` is `compensated`, `failed_needs_human` is `partial`, `pending` is `unknown`, and the three statuses that mean no step ran are `not_applied`.
- `type Recheck`: Runs current policy for an approved call just before it runs, after its pending request has verified.
- `type RejectionCause`: Why `verifyResolution()` refused.
- `interface RenderedOutcome`: A write outcome as the model reads it.
- `renderOutcome()`: Renders a write outcome for the model: sentences that name what happened, what to do next and what not to do, the outcome's fields as a JSON payload, and whether the provider's error flag should be set.
- `renderPlanOutcome()`: Renders a plan outcome for the model: `planWriteOutcome()` through `renderOutcome()`.
- `type Resolution`: A person's answer to a pending request: allow or deny for an approval, an answer for a clarification.
- `type ResolutionCheck`: What `verifyResolution()` returns: the resolution, once every check passed, or why it refused.
- `type Retry`: When the same write may run again.
- `runPlan()`: Runs the approved plan, in order, and reports what is true afterwards.
- `interface RunPlanOptions`: The options of `runPlan()`.
- `class SafetyError`: Thrown for a mistake in how the safety package is called, and, as its subclass `BudgetExceeded`, for a model call refused under a USD cap.
- `type SafetyErrorCode`: Why a `SafetyError` was thrown.
- `interface SignedPendingRequest`: A pause waiting for a person: an approval of one tool call, or a question about it.
- `signerFromKeyStore()`: Loads the ring from `store` and returns `hmacSigner()` over it.
- `signPending()`: Signs a pending request for a tool call.
- `interface SignPendingOptions`: Where `signPending()` takes its request id and time from.
- `signPlan()`: Signs a plan approval.
- `interface SignPlanOptions`: Where `signPlan()` takes its plan id and time from.
- `stateHash()`: Hashes the values a plan was computed from: the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (RFC 8785) of each value with its source and key, in order, under a fixed tag, as 64 lowercase hex digits.
- `interface StateRead`: A value the plan was computed from: where to read it, and under which key.
- `interface StateValue`: A value the plan read, with where it was read from.
- `type StepClass`: How a step behaves if the plan fails.
- `verifyPlanBeforeStep()`: Checks a plan approval before one of its steps runs, failing closed.
- `interface VerifyPlanStepOptions`: The options of `verifyPlanBeforeStep()`.
- `verifyResolution()`: Checks a resolution against its stored pending request before the call runs, failing closed.
- `interface VerifyResolutionOptions`: The options of `verifyResolution()`.
- `type WriteDedupe`: How a retry can find out what an earlier attempt of the write did.
- `writeOutcome()`: Builds a write outcome, filling in the defaults and checking every field.
- `type WriteOutcome`: What a write reports: one of the five kinds, with its retry rule and what the model should do next.
- `type WriteOutcomeInit`: The input to `writeOutcome()`.
- `type WriteOutcomeOf`: A write outcome of one kind, whose `retry` is one of the rules that kind allows.

## Exports from `@buildanagent/agent-safety/ai`

- `interface ApprovalRejection`: What `onRejected` receives when an approved call is denied.
- `type ApprovalRejectionCause`: Why `signedToolApproval()` denied an approved call: one of `verifyResolution()`'s causes, `unknown_request` when the store holds no pending request for the call, `policy_denied` when current policy or `recheck` said no, or `error` when a step threw.
- `repairInterruptedWrite()`: Returns `part` settled as `output-available` with an `unknown` write outcome as its output, if its tool is one of `writes` and `execute` may have started, or `undefined` for any other tool or a part still streaming its input or awaiting approval, so the caller keeps the default repair for those.
- `settleDeniedApprovals()`: Returns `messages` with every tool part whose call id is in `denied`, and whose state is still `approval-responded`, moved to `output-denied` with its approval marked `approved: false`, as `ai`'s UI message types and validator require for that state.
- `signedToolApproval()`: Wraps an approval policy so every approval is signed, fails closed on resume, and is checked against current policy before the approved call runs.
- `interface SignedToolApprovalOptions`: The options of `signedToolApproval()`.
- `toAiToolResult()`: Turns a write outcome into the result the model reads, for use as a tool's `toModelOutput`.

## Exports from `@buildanagent/agent-safety/byok`

- `assertNoDefaultProvider()`: Makes every string model id fail with a `SafetyError`, code `default_provider`, before any request.
- `explicitProvider()`: Builds an Anthropic provider on the user's key and base URL alone.
- `type ExplicitProviderName`: The providers `explicitProvider()` builds.
- `interface ExplicitProviderOptions`: The options of `explicitProvider()`.

## Exports from `@buildanagent/agent-safety/cost`

- `class BudgetExceeded`: Thrown by a cost guard instead of sending a model call.
- `budgetRefusal()`: The `BudgetExceeded` behind an error from `generateText`, `streamText` or an agent, or `undefined` when the error isn't a budget refusal.
- `type BudgetRefusalCode`: Why a call was refused: its projection would pass the cap, or its price is unknown, so the cap can't be checked.
- `interface BudgetRefusalInit`: What a refusal reports.
- `costGuard()`: A language-model middleware that caps what calls through it may spend.
- `interface CostGuardOptions`: Options for `costGuard()`.
- `interface FileRef`: A file a request points at, by URL or by provider reference, so the request holds none of its bytes.
- `type FileSize`: What the caller knows of a file's size: its bytes, or its pages.
- `type FileSizer`: Looks up the size of a file a request points at, or returns `undefined` when it isn't known.
- `type GuardableModel`: A language model the AI SDK accepts: a `LanguageModelV4`, `LanguageModelV3` or `LanguageModelV2`.
- `type GuardableProvider`: A provider the AI SDK accepts: a `ProviderV4`, `ProviderV3` or `ProviderV2`.
- `interface GuardedCall`: One call the guard let through, reported once its cost is known.
- `guardedModel()`: One model with `guards` around it, through the AI SDK's `wrapLanguageModel()`.
- `type GuardedModel`: A language model wrapped in guards: a `LanguageModelV4`.
- `guardedProvider()`: The provider with `guards` around each language model it returns, through the AI SDK's `wrapProvider()`.
- `type GuardedProvider`: A provider whose language models all run through the guards: a `ProviderV4`.
- `memorySpend()`: A `Spend` held in memory, starting at `initialUsd`, which lasts as long as the object does.
- `interface Spend`: The USD a run or session has spent on model calls so far.

## Exports from `@buildanagent/agent-safety/stores/cloudflare`

- `createCloudflareTables()`: Creates the two tables if they are not there, as every store of this module needs; call it once per object.
- `durableObjectEffectStore()`: An `EffectStore` on Durable Object SQLite.
- `durableObjectPlanLedger()`: A `PlanLedger` on Durable Object SQLite.
- `interface SqlCursorLike`: What a query returns here: the rows, and `RETURNING` makes the written ones count.
- `interface SqlStorageLike`: The part of `SqlStorage` (`ctx.storage.sql`) these stores use.

## Exports from `@buildanagent/agent-safety/stores/postgres`

- `createPostgresTables()`: Creates the two tables if they are not there.
- `interface PgClientLike`: The part of a Postgres client these stores use.
- `POSTGRES_SCHEMA`: The statements that create the two tables.
- `postgresEffectStore()`: An `EffectStore` on Postgres.
- `postgresPlanLedger()`: A `PlanLedger` on Postgres.

## Exports from `@buildanagent/agent-safety/stores/dynamodb`

- `dynamoEffectStore()`: An `EffectStore` on DynamoDB.
- `dynamoPlanLedger()`: A `PlanLedger` on DynamoDB.
- `interface DynamoStoreOptions`: The options of the DynamoDB stores.

## Exports from `@buildanagent/agent-safety/testing`

- `interface EffectStoreCase`: One conformance case: a name a test runner can show, and a check that rejects if the store breaks the rule.
- `effectStoreConformance()`: The cases every `EffectStore` must pass.
- `interface PlanLedgerCase`: One conformance case: a name a test runner can show, and a check that rejects if the ledger breaks the rule.
- `planLedgerConformance()`: The cases every `PlanLedger` must pass.
- `TEST_KEY_ID`: The key id of `testSigner()`.
- `testSigner()`: A signer with a fixed, published key, for tests and fixtures: every process produces the same signatures, so a signed pause can be checked into a test.
